author: opus 5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Closed: delivered in 'vibe-talk: keep the reply box's focus when a narrowed window hands it on late'. This was a real page bug, not the check reading focus too soon. The page decides one column or two in the frame after a resize, and hands a reply open in a column to the reply screen there, focusing the box only if it still has the focus. Chromium, once it has laid the narrower window out without the column, takes the focus off the box it no longer draws, in a task of its own, and a slow frame lets that task run first. The hand-off then found no focus and gave the keys to the reply screen's list. A reader narrowing a desktop window mid-sentence on a busy machine would lose the box the same way. The page now notes a focusout from the box that goes to nothing while the box is open in a column that is not drawn, and the hand-off gives the box the focus back as long as nothing else has had it since. Leaving the box for another element, or for nothing while it is still drawn, is the reader's own move and is not undone. Tests: reply_in_column_browser.py gains a slow-frame step for each column. It holds the page's requestAnimationFrame callbacks 250ms behind the browser's, checks first that the browser's focusout reached the box (still in its column) before any page frame ran, then requires the box to have the focus on the reply screen. voice_page.test.mjs gains a test of the quick-frame and slow-frame hand-offs in both columns and of a box the reader left themselves. It has two negative controls: the old hand-off loses the focus, and a note that is never cleared takes back a focus the reader had moved on from. Evidence, with 32 bounded busy loops pinned with the check to 8 CPUs: the unfixed check and page failed 2 of 30 runs with this issue's message, and the fixed ones passed 20 of 20. The new step fails every time against the unfixed page, unloaded and loaded, in either column, and the new page test fails against it too. validate --base github/main: OK. Unverified: only headless Chromium 149 on one host was tried. Firefox, Safari and a real desktop window resized by hand were not tested.
